facts.fact: StackAdapt's programmatic advertising glossary explains 47 common programmatic advertising terms.
facts.quote: Below, we’re explaining 47 of the most common, need-to-know programmatic advertising terms.

facts.fact: Under cost per mille (CPM) pricing, marketers pay a set price for every 1,000 impressions an ad receives.
facts.quote: marketers pay a set price for every 1,000 impressions that an ad receives

facts.fact: The StackAdapt glossary states that 'mille' is the Latin word for 'thousand', which is why cost per mille means cost per 1,000.
facts.quote: “Mille” is the latin word for “thousand,” which is why cost per mille means cost per 1,000.

facts.fact: StackAdapt's glossary defines click-through rate as the number of clicks an ad receives divided by the number of times the ad is shown.
facts.quote: CTR is the number of clicks that an ad receives, divided by the number of times that the ad is shown.

facts.fact: The StackAdapt glossary's CTR graphic shows CTR as clicks divided by impressions, multiplied by 100.
facts.quote: CTR = clicks divided by impressions, multiplied by 100.

facts.fact: StackAdapt's glossary defines cost per acquisition (CPA) as total campaign spend divided by the number of customers gained by that campaign.
facts.quote: CPA is calculated by dividing the total campaign spend by the number of customers that were gained by that campaign.

facts.fact: StackAdapt's glossary defines cost per click (CPC) as total ad cost divided by the number of clicks received.
facts.quote: CPC is calculated by dividing total ad cost by the number of clicks received.

facts.fact: StackAdapt's glossary defines cost per completed view (CPCV) as the campaign budget divided by the total completed views.
facts.quote: CPCV is calculated by dividing the budget of an ad campaign by the total completed views.

facts.fact: As an illustrative dayparting example, StackAdapt's glossary describes a marketer running ads on weekdays from 5pm to 9pm and on Saturdays from 12pm to 6pm.
facts.quote: a marketer might use dayparting to only run ads on weekdays between 5pm to 9pm and Saturdays 12pm to 6pm

facts.fact: According to the IAB, at least 50% of a display ad must be in view for at least one second for it to count as viewed.
facts.quote: at least 50% of an ad must be in view for at least one second for display ads and two seconds for video ads for them to count as being “viewed.”

facts.fact: StackAdapt's glossary states that real-time bidding auctions take less than a second.
facts.quote: the process happens in an instant auction that takes less than a second.

facts.fact: StackAdapt's glossary states that a view-through conversion window starts when the first impression is served and continues for a set number of days until a conversion occurs.
facts.quote: View-through conversions are tracked using a view-through conversion window, which starts as the first impression is served and continues until there is a conversion within a certain number of days.

facts.fact: StackAdapt's glossary defines programmatic direct (also called programmatic guaranteed) as a direct agreement between a publisher and advertiser made through a DSP-based buying system.
facts.quote: Programmatic direct, also known as programmatic guaranteed, is an agreement made directly between a publisher and an advertiser through a programmatic ad buying system like a demand-side platform (DSP).

facts.fact: StackAdapt's glossary says native outstream video ads only play when in view and stop playing if the user scrolls past them.
facts.quote: The video ads only play when they are in view. If a user scrolls past the native outstream video, it will stop playing.
